newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany targets computer kids with multimedia fair.
newsitem.headline: Germany targets computer kids with multimedia fair.

text.p: The world's leading consumer electronics and information technology firms are hosting a multimedia fair this week they hope will spark the imagination of youth in Europe's biggest technology market.
The CeBIT Home technology exhibition is expected to draw 150,000 mostly young visitors to attractions ranging from the latest television technology to virtual car races and Internet cafes.

Dazzled by the toys of the digital age by day and sustained at night by the beat of techno music, Germany's youth has been invited to ring in the Internet era and get cash registers ringing well ahead of the year-end shopping season.
"The CeBIT Home will be the most important source of orders for the industry, particularly for the Christmas business, in 1996," said Hubert Lange of trade fair group Deutsche Messe AG.

Some of the highlights of the fair will include new flat-screen television products and the first digital TV decoders that the industry hopes will bring a boost to home sales of home entertainment systems.
One of the central attractions is a multimedia screen measuring six by 90 metres (yards) that will project giant virtual rooms, computer animation, video clips and live events.

Much of what is being presented here is clearly targetted at the six to 17 age groups, those future leaders of the world who are no longer happy with simple casette players and have income of an estimated 5.4 billion marks ($3.7 billion) in Germany, according to a study by publishers Bastei, Springer und Bauer.
The focus on the young is also an admission that until now Germans have not been captured the Internet fever that has gripped the United States for the past two years.

Bernd Schiphorst, president of the New Media division of publishing giant Bertelsmann AG, said the company was working on integrating parts of the Internet into digital TV decoders in order to reach a broader public.
"Around 95 percent of the population does not even know what the Internet is. We want to provide them with their first impressions," he said.
Those who cannott make it to the CeBIT Home fair can see some of the attractions on the Internet at the following address: http://www.messe.de. ($1=1.4747 Mark)
